messages:
Emma: Quick sync — pushing a proposed decision. We need to lock the v1 commitments for Bridgework by EOD Friday so eng can schedule infra. My proposal: ship a narrow MVP on the original date (2026-04-20) with core routing + model pinning, but defer: tenant-config UI, full promptstore, and metrics dashboard to v1.0.1 post-launch. Thoughts?

Rahul: Sounds reasonable. The biggest risk is the KV cache migration + tenant config explosion. If we defer tenant UI we can avoid the large schema work and cut ~3 sprint weeks.

Maya: Agreed with Rahul. One ask: we still need a minimal API surface for tenants so infra can enforce per-tenant quotas. That can be a thin config object (no UI).

Emma: Yes — clarify: API-only tenant config (YAML/JSON via admin API) in MVP, UI in v1.0.1. Will update the PRD.

Carlos: Two checks: 1) customer-facing acceptance criteria for launch, and 2) can we commit to rollback/fallback if the model routing introduces latency >200ms P95? If either is hazy we should move date.

Rahul: For latency fallback we can implement a simple policy: if P95 > 200ms for 5m window, route to smaller model variant automatically. That adds ~2 days of work (policy + test).

Sam: Also add an SLO for error budget burn. I can wire a temporary alert: route-fallback-triggered > 0 should page on call when in beta.

Jenna: From design POV: deferring tenant UI is OK. But we should include a minimal copy/placeholder in admin to avoid empty states when marketing demos the product. I can ship a static mock that hits the admin API.

Emma: Proposal updated: MVP scope = routing, model pinning, admin API tenant config, minimal static admin placeholder, canary rollout plan, latency fallback policy. Defer: tenant UI, full promptstore, metrics dashboard, advanced quantization profiles.

Rahul: What about telemetry for quality regressions? We need a small eval harness or we risk rolling back due to quality drift.

Emma: Add a lightweight eval runner that runs a core prompt set on canary traffic and fails the rollout on regression >5% on key metrics. Keep it minimal (no large infra).

Maya: ETA check: with the reduced scope, engineering estimates shrink from 6 to 4 sprints. Ops work for canary and fallback ~1 sprint. That maps to our target.

Carlos: Ok, decision vote — quick thumbs: commit to MVP on 2026-04-20 with the updated reduced scope and the safety policies (latency fallback + eval harness + SLO alerting) and defer other items to v1.0.1.

Emma: @channel please react with :thumbsup: if you approve, :thumbsdown: if you object. I'll collect and post a cut-decision doc.

Rahul: :thumbsup:

Maya: :thumbsup:

Jenna: :thumbsup:

Sam: :thumbsup:

Carlos: :thumbsup:

Emma: Cool — decision recorded. Action items: 1) Emma to update PRD & release checklist (today). 2) Rahul/Maya to rebaseline sprint plan (tomorrow). 3) Sam to add SLO alerting and temporary page policy (this week). 4) Jenna to provide static admin stub (this week). 5) Carlos to notify sales FRR about deferred features and compensation plan (this week).

deploy-bot: deployment pipeline check: next canary window available 2026-04-15 08:00 UTC — schedule after infra changes merged.

Emma: I'll post the cut-decision doc in Confluence and ping the sales thread. Thanks all.

Rahul: One more: add a simple migration plan note in the PRD for the KV cache change so oncall isn't surprised.

Emma: Good call—I'll add that. Done.
